name: Eli
bio:
Eli was the priest at Shiloh, mentor and caretaker of the young Samuel, whose failure to restrain his two wicked sons, Hophni and Phinehas, ultimately brought severe judgment upon his entire family.

When Hannah prayed with deep anguish at the Shiloh sanctuary, Eli, not understanding, first mistook her for drunk, then blessed her once she explained herself (1 Samuel 1:9-18). After Hannah brought the weaned Samuel to Eli to serve the LORD for life, Eli, now old, heard repeatedly how his sons committed detestable acts among the people — sleeping with women who served at the tent of meeting and seizing sacrificial meat by force — and though he rebuked them, they would not listen (1 Samuel 2:12-25). A man of God came and warned Eli that the LORD would judge his whole house, that his two sons Hophni and Phinehas would die on the same day, and promised to raise up a faithful priest to replace Eli's line (1 Samuel 2:27-36).

When the LORD called out to the young Samuel three times in the night, Eli recognized it was the LORD calling and instructed Samuel how to respond; the next day, when Samuel told him the LORD's words of judgment against his house, Eli simply said, "He is the LORD; let him do what is good in his eyes" (1 Samuel 3:1-18), showing that despite his age and weakness, he still submitted to the LORD's sovereignty. Eli judged Israel for forty years, serving as the key figure bridging the era of the judges and the book of Samuel; the tragic conclusion of his later years would unfold further in the account of Israel's war with the Philistines and the capture of the ark.
